newsitem.title: USA: Cold, wet weather further delays Iowa corn seeding.
newsitem.headline: Cold, wet weather further delays Iowa corn seeding.

text.p: Cold and wet weather again delayed spring fieldwork and corn seedings in Iowa during the week ended Sunday, according to the Iowa Agricultural Statistical Reporting Service.
Snow from last weekend's storm melted from Iowa fields, but it still delayed field work until late in the week. Soil temperatures have not risen enough to ensure germination.
Oat seedings stood at 53 percent complete, above the 38 percent of a week ago but behind the year ago pace of 57 percent and the average of 57 percent.
Topsoil moisture levels were 21 percent surplus, 78 percent adequate and one percent short.
A snowstorm in the state a week ago slowed fieldwork, but the greatest impact was on the state's livestock herd.

The statistical reporting board said reporters in every district reported calf losses or disease related to the winter-like weather. The most significant losses were experienced in the south central and southeast districts where the heaviest snow fell.
